questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to go somewhere with my friends where we could experience another culture together and see what it’s like to attend school in Italy instead of Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult at first. You have to create your own class schedule, and it took us several hours because many of the classes overlap. It’s also hard to understand the exam formats, and the meeting times are more or less decided by the teachers as they go. There’s a very ‘we’ll figure it out’ approach, whereas in Denmark you’re used to a much stricter structure.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wrote a lot of emails back and forth to the teachers because I was missing information. During the first week here, you can also go to as many classes as you want to find the ones that fit you. The first week with the class schedule is very confusing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Airbnb, where I messaged a lot of people on the platform and then ended up making an arrangement outside the platform

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The Italian people like to "meet you" before entering into a contract; they are more interested in a good personality (especially if it’s a private landlord through Airbnb). I had tons of phone calls and facetime session before booking the right thing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, it’s very confusing. It’s really a puzzle that has to fit together. We also ended up with more schoolwork than we’ve ever had in Denmark. You start by attending a lot of different classes to find the right ones, after first trying to see which courses are offered and how they are scheduled. Then you ‘shop around’ between classes during the first two weeks. Depending on your courses, you might already have your first exam early on, it depends on whether you are an attending or non-attending student. Throughout the semester, you have ongoing exams, and in some courses you also finish with a final exam. Registration for exams opens 2–3 weeks before the exam date, so you need to remember that as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There’s no organizational support, but the teachers are very kind and helpful. It almost seems like they’re used to getting a lot of questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn’t end up with the courses I initially thought I would take. There was an overlap in the schedule, so I had to find some others.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you’re in doubt, just send an email to the teacher listed for the course. They are very helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Going to school here is different from back home. The expectations are different, and my impression is that people have very mixed feelings about whether it’s harder or easier. For me personally, this has been the most demanding semester of my entire studies, because we had exams every other week, so there was constant reading, whereas I’m used to everything being concentrated at the end. I wouldn’t say the academic level is difficult, but I still haven’t figured out their grading system

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I probably prefer the Danish system, but my impression was that there were also many Danish students who felt comfortable with the way schooling and exams work down here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is this option where you can join ESN, which I think is organized by some students. You pay a one-time fee (around 15 euros, I think), and then you can take part in lots of activities that are posted continuously in a WhatsApp group. I didn’t use it myself, but I can see how it could be beneficial for students to meet this way.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN club as mentioned before.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to COMO!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One difference that many of us Danish students have talked about is that all the Italians just talk during class. It feels very disrespectful and was something we didn’t expect people to do.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, and sharing a bottle of wine in the evening with my friends in beautiful surroundings.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check your alumni email

Keep yourself updated on the Mobility Online portal

Do good research on courses before you come here, it will help you when you need to register

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with my closest friends and experiencing another culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It’s always good to be challenged when it comes to speaking English and presenting, so I’ve found it nerve-racking but beneficial in the long run.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
